insights: Campanhã departures split into two recurrent corridors, east toward place A and west toward place B.
The place A corridor is served by a smaller recurring driver group, while the place B corridor involves a broader taxi pool.
Place A trips are more common earlier in the day, while place B trips become more prominent during late afternoon and evening.
Taxi-stand trips dominate both corridors, but street-hail trips form a larger evening share on the place B branch.
summary: Campanhã trips follow distinct eastward and westward branches. The eastern place A branch has a smaller recurrent driver group and is relatively earlier, while place B draws a broader pool, becomes prominent later, and has a larger evening street-hail share.
